bug_semantics: The public POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and API key, then made server-side requests and returned the remote JSON response or selected event data. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but treated every syntactically ordinary hostname as safe without DNS resolution. A hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address therefore bypassed the guard, allowing an anonymous network caller to make cti-transmute reach an internal HTTPS service and disclose its response. The direct fix resolves domain names, requires every resulting address to be globally routable, and requires authentication on both routes.
flaw_origin: Direct source introduction: b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 added the flawed hostname validator and both unauthenticated server-side fetch routes together in website/web/convert/convert.py; it was not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, or reconstructed squash member.
evidence: First-party advisory page https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x373-32xc-7gqv identifies CVE-2026-73160/GHSA-x373-32xc-7gqv, the two routes, hostname-without-resolution bypass, anonymous response disclosure, and fix commit 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512; it reports package affected/patched versions as Unknown.

At b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48, `git show b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48:website/web/convert/convert.py` shows _validate_misp_url at lines 15-32: lines 26-31 check only IP literals and `except ValueError: pass  # it's a domain name — OK`. Lines 133-186 add unauthenticated /fetch_misp_event, call requests.get on the caller's URL, and return resp.text; lines 189-272 add unauthenticated /misp_search_events, call requests.post on the caller's URL, and return parsed event fields. Neither route has @login_required.

`git log -L ':_validate_misp_url:website/web/conversions/conversions.py'` follows the same function through the path rename and shows its first addition in b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48, an unchanged unsafe-domain branch through later history, and its replacement only in 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512. `git log -L ':fetch_misp_event:website/web/conversions/conversions.py'` likewise reaches the route's zero-line addition in b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48. `git log --all -S"pass  # it's a domain name — OK" --format='%H %P %s' --name-status --` returns only b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 as addition and 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 as removal, cross-checking the smallest origin.

Direct parent verification: `git show 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5:website/web/convert/convert.py` contains zero occurrences of `_validate_misp_url`, `/fetch_misp_event`, and `/misp_search_events`; `git show --patch b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 -- website/web/convert/convert.py` shows all three constructs as additions against that immediate parent.

Direct fix verification: parent 957c56bdc64bfbbf9fafacc9a410dcbf32371cfd still has the unsafe `except ValueError: pass` at website/web/conversions/conversions.py:47-64 and no login decorators at route lines 237-238 and 314-315. `git show 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 -- website/web/conversions/conversions.py` adds socket.getaddrinfo-based _resolved_ips, changes validation to reject an empty result or any address for which is_global is false, and adds @login_required to both routes. The commit is a one-parent direct source fix, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha coincide.

Git version boundary: `git tag --contains b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` returns v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, while `git tag --contains 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512` returns only v1.5. `git for-each-ref --sort=creatordate --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname) %(creatordate:iso-strict)' refs/tags` places v1.2 before the introducer, v1.3/v1.4 after the introducer but before the fix, and v1.5 after the fix. Thus the Git-tag-derived affected releases are v1.3 and v1.4 and the first fixed release is v1.5, notwithstanding the advisory's Unknown version fields.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` shows author and committer `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>`, parent 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5, subject `add: [misp connection] can connect to a misp instance and select event to import`, and no message body, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker. No later commit's signal was used.
reasoning: The exploitable mechanism begins only when a request sink and a bypassable destination guard coexist. The same direct commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 first wrote both affected anonymous routes and the validator branch that automatically accepts DNS hostnames, while its immediate parent has none of them. Later renames and the MISP transport-helper refactor preserve rather than originate the flaw. Commit 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 closes both causal dimensions by vetting all resolved addresses and adding login gates. Tag containment proves v1.3-v1.4 vulnerable and v1.5 fixed. Because the required judgment is limited to the BIC commit object and that object has a human identity and no AI attribution/generation marker, the supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.
